The study published in the American Journal of Occupational Therapy (2016) focused on accessibility improvements for housing as per WHO guidelines, emphasizing accessibility rather than health outcomes. 2. Hagen et al. (2007) explored the use and effectiveness of assistive technology for individuals with dementia in Ireland, highlighting its role in fostering independence. This was published in Technology & Disability. 3. Hanson and Percival (2005) investigated the housing and support needs of visually impaired adults in England, without reporting specific outcomes. This was published in the British Journal of Visual Impairment. 4. Horvath et al. (2013) conducted a clinical trial on a home safety toolkit for Alzheimer's disease, assessing caregivers' ability to create a safe home environment. This was published in the International Journal of Alzheimer Disease. 5. Hutchings et al. (2008) studied the impact of home modifications on older adults with developmental disabilities living in group homes or supported apartments. This was published in the Journal of Housing for the Elderly. 6. Novak and Lannin (2009) conducted a double-blind, randomized controlled trial on occupational therapy home programs for children with cerebral palsy, though accessibility interventions were not described. This was published in Pediatrics. 7. Iwarsson (2005) examined the long-term relationship between person-environment fit and ADL (activities of daily living) dependence among older Swedish adults. This was published in The Gerontologist. 8. Iwarsson and Wilson (2006) described functional limitations and environmental barriers among older adults in Sweden, focusing on housing satisfaction and accessibility. This was published in Technology and Disability. 9. Johansson et al. (2009) conducted a qualitative study on the experiences of four adults during the housing adaptation process, emphasizing the role of environmental barriers in aging in place. This was published in Aging & Society. 10. Kaminsky (2008) explored perceived environmental barriers and supports for individuals with low vision due to diabetic retinopathy, using ICF domains to assess environmental factors. This was published in Dissertation Abstracts International. 11. Kaminsky et al. (2014) conducted a qualitative study on environmental supports and barriers experienced by individuals with vision loss from diabetes, using ICF domains for analysis. This was published in Disability & Rehabilitation. 12. Kutintara et al. (2013) designed and evaluated a kitchen tailored for individuals with visual impairments. This was published in Disability. 13. La Grow et al. (2006) discussed a program that successfully reduced fall-related hazards in individuals aged 75 and older with significant visual impairments. This was published in Injury Prevention. 14. Linskell and Hill (2010) studied the role of smart home technology in enhancing supported living for individuals with complex needs and challenging behaviors. This was published in the Journal of Assistive Technologies. 15. Tomita et al. (2007) conducted a randomized controlled trial on the use of smart home technology, including remote controls, motion sensors, and security systems, for frail older adults. This was published in Topics in Geriatric Rehabilitation. 16. Markle-Reid et al. (2007) designed a randomized controlled trial using a multifactorial and interdisciplinary team approach to reduce fall risk in frail older home-care clients. Home accessibility interventions were not described. This was published in the Journal of Patient Safety. 17. Marquardt et al. (2011) conducted a cross-sectional study on home modifications for individuals with dementia and the barriers to implementation. This was published in the Journal of Housing for the Elderly. 18. McCullagh (2006) provided an informative paper on how to help patients make their homes safer and more accessible as their abilities change. This was published in the American Journal of Nursing. 19. Metzeltin et al. (2010) studied primary care interventions for frail older adults, without describing the accessibility component. This was published in BMC Public Health. 20. Nilsson and Iwarsson (2013) developed a protocol for a longitudinal cohort study on the home environment for individuals with Parkinson’s disease, with planned follow-up over three years. Results were not yet available. This was published in BMC Neurology. 21. Nishita et al. (2007) analyzed patterns in the diffusion of visitability legislation to promote basic home accessibility. This was published in the Journal of Disability Policy Studies. 22. Novak (2011) conducted a systematic review of home-based interventions for adults, without describing home accessibility interventions. This was published in Clinical Rehabilitation. 23. Nygard et al. (2008) studied the provision of stove timing devices for individuals with cognitive impairments. This was published in the Scandinavian Journal of Occupational Therapy. 24. Ormerod (2008) reviewed a book on accessible housing, focusing on quality, disability, and design. This was published in Ergonomics. 25. Ostensjo et al. (2005) conducted a cross-sectional study on the use and impact of assistive devices and environmental modifications on everyday activities and care in young children with cerebral palsy. This was published in Disability & Rehabilitation. 26. Percival and Hanson (2007) conducted a mixed-method study on accommodation types and access to housing for visually impaired individuals. This was published in the British Journal of Visual Impairment. 27. Pettersson et al. (2012) conducted a longitudinal mixed-methods study on clients’ experiences of the housing adaptation process. This was published in Disability & Rehabilitation. 28. Prellwitz and Skar (2006) studied how children with restricted mobility perceive the accessibility and usability of their home environment. This was published in Occupational Therapy International. 29. Pynoos et al. (2010) discussed environmental assessment and modification as fall-prevention strategies for older adults. This was published in Clinics in Geriatric Medicine. 30. Reid (2004) studied the accessibility and usability of the physical housing environment for stroke survivors. This was published in the International Journal of Rehabilitation Research. 31. Reid (2004) also examined the impact of the environment on role performance in older stroke survivors living at home. This was published in the International Journal of Therapy & Rehabilitation. 32. Riazi et al. (2012) studied home modification guidelines recommended by visually impaired individuals. This was published in the Journal of Assistive Technologies. 33. Riikonen et al. (2010) studied safety and monitoring technologies for the homes of individuals with dementia. This was published in Gerontechnology. 34. Roessler et al. (2013) studied the specialized housing and transportation needs of adults with multiple sclerosis. This was published in Work. 35. Rosenberg et al. (2012) studied environmental restrictions at home, in the community, and in educational settings, and their impact on the participation of children with developmental disabilities. This was published in Child: Care, Health & Development. 36. Roy et al. (2008) conducted a qualitative study on parents’ experiences of the home adaptation process for children with motor disabilities. This was published in Physical & Occupational Therapy in Pediatrics. 37. Shyu et al. (2004) studied environmental barriers and mobility in Taiwan, applying the Roy adaptation model. This was published in Nursing Science Quarterly. 38. Steultjens and Clemson (2006) commented on a preventative home safety program for older individuals with low vision, which reduced falls and was more cost-effective than an exercise program. This was published in the Australian Occupational Therapy Journal. 39. Stineman et al. (2011) studied the association between ADL staging, chronic health conditions, and perceived lack of home accessibility features in elderly community-dwelling individuals. This was published in the Journal of the American Geriatrics Society. 40. Stineman et al. (2012) examined the relationship between physical home and social environments, ADL limitations, and nursing home use among older adults. This was published in the Archives of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation. 41. Szanton et al. (2011) conducted a pilot study on the CAPABLE program for low-income older adults with ADL/IADL difficulties, which included handyman visits but did not focus on accessibility modifications. This was published in the Journal of the American Geriatrics Society. 42. Torrington (2009) studied the design of technology and environments to support enjoyable activities for individuals with dementia. This was published in ALTER, European Journal of Disability. 43. Van Hoof and Kort (2009) presented a conceptual paper on designing dwellings for older adults with dementia. This was published in Dementia. 44. Van Hoof et al. (2010) reviewed focus group discussions on home environments for individuals with dementia. This was published in the American Journal of Alzheimer’s Disease & Other Dementias. 45. Wahl et al. (2009) studied the relationship between home environments, modifications, and disability-related outcomes in older adults. This was published in The Gerontologist. 46. Werngren-Elgström et al. (2008) conducted a 10-year longitudinal study on the relationship between ADL dependence and person-environment fit among older Swedish adults. This was published in Aging Clinical & Experimental Research. 47. Werngren-Elgström et al. (2009) also studied the relationship between subjective well-being, ADL dependence, and person-environment fit in older adults. This was published in the Archives of Gerontology & Geriatrics. 48. York (2009) discussed residential design and outdoor area accessibility, including related legislation. This was published in NeuroRehabilitation. 49. Young (2012) provided an informative paper on effective home modifications for clients with low vision. This was published in OT Practice.
